relationship: A rounded measurement represents an interval, and calculated bounds must use the extremal values that make the stated claim hardest to certify.

learnerLoop.action: Scrub true readings to discover rounding boundaries, drag distance and time to find speed extremes, prove the claim, then test finer measurements.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Rounded displays change as true values cross interval endpoints; dragging allowed distance and time updates the derived speed.
learnerLoop.evidence: The interval model, extremal case and certification check reveal whether the claim follows.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Choose the upper or lower bound that tests the claim conservatively.

invariants: A rounded value includes all values in its rounding interval.
A guarantee requires the extremal case that works against the claim.
safeAdaptations: Vary rounding units and positive measurement scenarios.
Adjust calculation support while retaining boundary discovery, direct speed exploration, the worst-case proof and the finer-precision comparison.
nonGoals: Certifying a claim from the rounded displayed values alone.
